info.title: tempr
info.description: Tempr CLI -- sign in, chat, and run agentic coding tasks from the terminal.

commands.name: acp
commands.description:
Run as an Agent Client Protocol agent for an editor such as Zed or JetBrains AI
Assistant, over stdin and stdout.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --version
options.description: Prints version information

commands.name: auth
commands.description: Sign in with a Tempr license key.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --version
options.description: Prints version information

options.name: --browser
options.description:
Sign in through your browser without asking how: show a
code to approve on the Tempr portal, from any device

arguments.name: LICENSEKEY
arguments.description:
Your Tempr license key. Omit it to sign in through your
browser or paste the key at a prompt, so it doesn't end up
in shell history

commands.name: chat
commands.description: Send one message or start an interactive session (also the default command).

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --version
options.description: Prints version information

options.name: --model
options.description:
Model id to use for this run (overrides
'tempr config set-model'). Run 'tempr
models' to see what your licence is
entitled to

options.name: --verbose
options.description:
Print each tool call's full output, and
the token usage (prompt/completion/total,
and cost if known) after each turn

options.name: --json
options.description:
Emit newline-delimited JSON (one RunEvent
per line) instead of formatted text -- for
scripting

options.name: --yolo
options.description:
Run unattended: auto-approve file edits,
MCP calls and allow-listed commands for
this run (approval-mode=autopilot for this
invocation only). On Linux its commands
run in the sandbox by default, with the
network on, so any command goes ahead;
elsewhere, commands that aren't
allow-listed are still refused without a
terminal to ask on, and ones that delete,
publish or force-push always are

options.name: --ask
options.description:
Plain single-turn chat with no
tool-calling

options.name: --id
options.description:
Resume a saved session by id (see 'tempr
history'). A new id is generated and saved
automatically if omitted

options.name: --continue
options.description:
Resume the most recent session started in
this folder

options.name: --max-turns
options.description:
Stop after N steps of the agent loop.
Guards an unattended run against a model
that won't converge; the server clamps it
to your plan's ceiling

options.name: --allowed-tools
options.description:
Comma-separated tool names this run may
use, e.g. 'read_file,search_files'. An MCP
server's name covers all of its tools.
Everything else is left out of the
manifest entirely

options.name: --disallowed-tools
options.description:
Comma-separated tool names this run may
not use, applied after --allowed-tools

options.name: --approval-mode
options.description:
Approval mode for this run only:
interactive, autopilot or bypass.
Overrides the saved mode without changing
it; --yolo is shorthand for autopilot

options.name: --reasoning
options.description:
How much the model reasons for this run:
none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh,
max, on, or default. Overrides the level
saved with /reasoning, for this invocation
only; a level the model lacks becomes the
nearest one it has

options.name: --prompt-file
options.description:
Read the message from a file instead of
the command line -- for prompts too long
or too quote-heavy to pass as an argument

options.name: --search
options.description:
Let the model search the web through its
provider (Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI
models), billed per search. On by default
at a terminal, off for --json and piped
runs

options.name: --no-search
options.description:
Don't let the model search the web for
this run. 'tempr config set-web-search
off' turns it off for every run
from the cost each call reports,
sub-agents included, across every turn of
a session. Exits with code 6. A model
whose price isn't known can't be counted,
and the CLI says so

options.name: --max-cost
options.description:
Stop once this run's model calls have cost
this many US dollars, e.g. 0.50 -- counted
from the cost each call reports,
sub-agents included, across every turn of
a session. Exits with code 6. A model
whose price isn't known can't be counted,
and the CLI says so

options.name: --sandbox
options.description:
Run the agent's commands in a sandbox
(Linux): they can change only this folder,
the temp folders and the package caches,
and can't reach the network. Any command
then runs without asking, except ones that
delete, publish or force-push. If the
sandbox can't run here, nothing runs (exit
code 7)

options.name: --sandbox-network
options.description:
Like --sandbox, with the network left on
inside it

options.name: --no-sandbox
options.description:
Don't sandbox this run's commands,
whatever 'tempr config set-sandbox' says,
and not by default with --yolo or in CI
either

arguments.name: PROMPT
arguments.description:
The message to send. Omit to start the interactive REPL, or pipe
stdin for headless mode

commands.name: completion
commands.description: Print a shell completion script: bash, zsh, fish or powershell.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --version
options.description: Prints version information

arguments.name: SHELL
arguments.description: bash, zsh, fish or powershell

commands.name: config
commands.description: View or change CLI configuration (~/.tempr/config.json, or --config <path>).

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

commands.name: allow-command
commands.description: Add a persistent run_command allow-list prefix.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

arguments.name: PREFIX
arguments.description:
A command prefix to allow without confirmation, e.g. 'aws s3'.
Persisted to ~/.tempr/config.json

commands.name: allow-site
commands.description:
Let web_fetch open pages on a site without asking: docs.example.com, or
*.example.com for its subdomains.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

arguments.name: SITE
arguments.description:
A site to open without asking: 'docs.example.com', or
'*.example.com' for every subdomain

commands.name: disallow-command
commands.description: Remove a run_command allow-list prefix.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

arguments.name: PREFIX
arguments.description:
A previously allowed command prefix to remove, exactly as it was
added

commands.name: disallow-site
commands.description: Remove a site added with allow-site.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

arguments.name: SITE
arguments.description: A previously allowed site to remove

commands.name: set-approval-mode
commands.description:
Set the default approval mode: interactive (confirm everything), autopilot
(unattended; only destructive or non-allow-listed commands ask), or bypass (file
edits run, every command asks).

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

arguments.name: MODE
arguments.description:
One of: interactive (confirm every mutating tool call), autopilot
(auto-approve file edits, MCP calls and allow-listed commands;
still confirm destructive and non-allow-listed ones -- this is the
unattended mode, and what --yolo uses), bypass (auto-approve file
edits, but confirm every command and MCP call -- stricter than
autopilot, despite the name)

commands.name: set-crash-reports
commands.description:
Turn crash reports on or off. Off until you're asked; a report carries the error
type and message, the stack trace, the CLI version and your OS version.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

commands.name: set-model
commands.description: Set the default model used when --model is omitted.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

arguments.name: MODELID
arguments.description:
Model id to use whenever --model is omitted. See your Tempr
account portal for available model ids

commands.name: set-notifications
commands.description: Turn the bell and desktop notification after a long turn on or off.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

commands.name: set-sandbox
commands.description:
Run the agent's commands in a sandbox (Linux): on (no network), network (network
on), off, or auto (the default: --yolo and CI runs, with the network on).
--sandbox, --sandbox-network and --no-sandbox decide for one run.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

commands.name: set-web-search
commands.description:
Turn the model's web search on or off for interactive runs (Anthropic, OpenAI
and xAI models, billed per search). Scripts search only with --search.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show the current configuration.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

commands.name: doctor
commands.description:
Check config, sign-in, server connectivity, the model catalog and MCP servers.
Exits non-zero if anything fails, so a CI job can gate on it.

options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --version
options.description: Prints version information

options.name: --skip-mcp
options.description:
Don't start the configured MCP servers. They can take
several seconds each; skip when you only want the local
and account checks

options.description: Prints help information

arguments.name: SESSIONID
arguments.description: A session id, as shown by 'tempr history list'

commands.name: fork
commands.description: Copy a saved session under a new id, to take it in a second direction.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List this folder's saved sessions (--all for every folder's).

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --all
options.description: List sessions from every folder, not just this one

commands.name: rename
commands.description: Give a saved session a new title.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

arguments.name: SESSIONID
arguments.description: A session id, as shown by 'tempr history list'

arguments.name: TITLE
arguments.description: The new title. Quote it if it contains spaces

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show a saved session's conversation.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

arguments.name: SESSIONID
arguments.description: A session id, as shown by 'tempr history list'

commands.name: init
commands.description: Draft an AGENTS.md for this workspace from a scan of what's in it.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --version
options.description: Prints version information

options.name: --force
options.description: Overwrite an existing AGENTS.md instead of refusing

options.name: --print
options.description: Write the draft to stdout instead of to a file

commands.name: keys
commands.description: List, add or remove the API keys Tempr uses to call each model provider for you.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

commands.name: add
commands.description:
Add or replace a provider's key: typed at a hidden prompt, piped in, or read
with --from-env. Never passed as an argument.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --from-env
options.description:
Read the key from this environment variable
instead of prompting -- for scripts and CI.
Piping the key in on standard input works too

options.name: --force
options.description:
Save the key even if the provider rejects it
when it's checked

arguments.name: PROVIDER
arguments.description:
The provider the key is for, e.g. openai, anthropic, google.
Omit it to pick from a list

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the providers you have a key for (also plain 'tempr keys').

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Remove a provider's key.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

arguments.name: PROVIDER
arguments.description: The provider whose key to remove, e.g. openai

commands.name: logout
commands.description: Sign out and clear the stored session.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --version
options.description: Prints version information

commands.name: mcp
commands.description: Manage MCP servers (~/.tempr/mcp.json).

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

commands.name: add
commands.description:
Add or update an MCP server. Usage: tempr mcp add <name> --cwd <dir> --env
KEY=VALUE -- <command> args...

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --cwd
options.description:
Working directory to launch the server process in
(defaults to the current directory)

options.name: --env
options.description:
Environment variable to set for the server process.
Repeatable, e.g. --env API_KEY=abc123

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description:
A short local name for this server (used to
enable/disable/remove it later)

arguments.name: COMMAND
arguments.description: The executable to launch the server with, e.g. 'npx'

arguments.name: ARGS
arguments.description:
Arguments passed to the command, e.g. '-y
@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem .'

commands.name: browse
commands.description: Browse and install a server from the curated MCP catalog.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

arguments.name: QUERY
arguments.description:
Optional search term (matches name, description, publisher, and
tags). Omit to browse the full catalog

commands.name: disable
commands.description: Disable an MCP server.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The server's local name, as shown by 'tempr mcp list'

options.name: --help

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The server's local name, as shown by 'tempr mcp list'

commands.name: list
commands.description: List configured MCP servers.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Remove an MCP server.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The server's local name, as shown by 'tempr mcp list'

commands.name: update
commands.description: Check for a newer release and say how to install it.

options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --version

options.name: --check
options.description:
Only report whether a newer version exists; don't install
anything. Exits 0 when up to date, 1 when an update is
